title: Raincheck Overnight Sketches: post-incident handoff
content:
Quick context: overnight I was covering US-West and ran into two related outages — a latency spike impacting /v1/generate on hosted-api and a KV-cache desync that made tail latency burst on long-context requests. This is a rough, run-anywhere scratchpad for the next shift. Not tidy.

Shift summary (11/18 22:00 PST -> 11/19 06:30 PST)
- 22:05: Alerts: p95 latency > 1.8s on hosted-api (us-west) — customer-facing errors started to creep up.
- 22:12: Spikes correlated with a batch of long-context requests from a single heavy-tenant (acct: acme-marketing).
- 22:30: While investigating, observed KV cache miss rate jump from 2% -> 42% for serving runtime group-3 nodes.
- 22:45: Rolled a partial routing rule to fallback to model-variant small-gpt-3-compat for the heavy tenant; latency improved but token-cost increased.
- 01:10: Found a scheduled config push from deployments pipeline (PR #893) that changed cache-ttl from 6h -> 30m on group-3 — appears to have caused sudden churn.
- 03:00: Reverted TTL change for group-3; cache-miss slowly returned to baseline by 03:40.
- 04:10: Noted degraded QoS for long-context streaming (some clients saw cut streams) — edge case with partial resend logic and retry loop.
- 05:20: Applied temporary fix: enabled aggressive prefix-caching for streaming routes for 1h.

What I ran (commands & pointers)
- k8s: kubectl -n inference get pods -l runtime=group-3 -o wide
- logs: gcloud logging read "resource.labels.cluster_name=redwood-inference AND labels.node_group=group-3" --limit 200 --format json > /tmp/group3-logs.json
- feature toggle rollback: curl -X POST $FEATURE_SVC/toggle -d '{"name":"cache-ttl-group3","value":"6h"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- routing override: post to control-plane /routing/overrides {"tenant":"acme-marketing","route":"small-gpt-3-compat","window":"30m"} (used console when curl flaked out)

Immediate runbook (short, for whoever picks up)
1) Monitor: grafana -> SLOs -> hosted-api/us-west -> watch p50/p95/p99 and error-rate. Set dashboard to 5m refresh.
2) If p95 > 1.5s or error-rate > 0.5%:
   - Check KV cache miss ratio (metric: runtime.cache.miss_ratio) for node groups (group-1..group-4).
   - If miss_ratio > 20% for any group: temporarily raise TTL for that group back to 6h via feature toggle and force cache warm (see warming step).
3) Warming step (if you change TTL): run a warm-up job that replays top-20 prefixes from the hot tenant: python tools/cache_warm.py --tenant acme-marketing --prefixes 20 --target group-3
4) If cache rollback is not possible (toggle endpoint failing): consider routing override to small-gpt-3-compat for the offending tenant(s) for 30-60m.
5) For streaming cutoff symptoms (partial stream/resend loops): increase streaming buffer flush interval to 500ms for 30m via console (path: console -> runtime -> streaming -> buffer-ms).

Temporary mitigations we used (notes)
- Routing override to small variant for acme-marketing (effective immediate latency drop). Pros: quick. Cons: higher token usage, perceptual quality drop reported by one QA.
- Manual TTL rollback (feature toggle) — fixed root cause but rollout was messy because config pipeline retried and re-applied the bad value once. Need pipeline lock.

Open/unfinished items (TODO for next shift or SRE follow-up)
- Chase down pipeline retry: PR #893 merged but CI re-applied value during the window. Who owns the deploy-automation job? (Assign to infra/deployments)
- Make cache-ttl opt changes gate-protected for node-groups: create a safelist/approval job.
- Add an automated warm-up job triggered after TTL reductions to avoid cold bursts.
- Reproduce streaming partial-send locally: capture a reproducible request sequence and file a bug to serving-runtime backlog.

Notes-to-self: weird behaviors seen
- node group-3 (older A100 fleet) had slightly higher GC pauses in the runtime which aggravated prefix cache misses — not sure if it is memory pressure or kernel-level CPU steal.
- Observed 8x retry traffic from our internal client-side SDK when streaming failures triggered — amplification risk.

Customer impact & comms
- ACME: minor user-facing latency, one support ticket opened (SUP-1228). We provided a temporary mitigation (routing to smaller model) and follow-up that TTL revert performed. Please keep CS looped (Priya is on the thread).

Suggested post-mortem outline (short)
- Timeline with config push and TTL change (PR #893)
- Why TTL change occurred (root cause: automation/CI retry)
- Impact metrics (p95, error-rate, cache-miss spike)
- Mitigations (routing override, TTL rollback, warm-up)
- Action items: deploy pipeline lock, warm-up automation, streaming resilience ticket.

Quick links
- Logs dump: gs://redwood-dumps/oncall/2024-11-18/group3-logs.json (uploaded)
- JIRA: JIRA-4721 (incident) / JIRA-4723 (streaming retry bug)
- Slack: #sre-ops thread ts:1700304000.000200

For the morning handoff (explicit)
- Note: I left the routing override in place for acme-marketing until 07:30 PST to avoid thrash. If you lift it, do it gradually and observe cache-miss for group-3 immediately.
- If errors drop to baseline and miss_ratio < 5% for 10m, remove override and monitor for 30m before marking incident resolved.

Random scribbles / ideas for reduce-repeat:
- Add a deploy-run checklist that blocks TTL changes without a warm-up stage.
- Add a synthetic tenant that simulates long-context streaming traffic to catch these cases in pre-prod.

End of sketch. Ping me on slack (maya.k) if anything smells off or you need command help.

-- maya
